lessons.title: The dead contribute nothing
lessons.teach: The text says we were dead, not sick. A sick man can cooperate with treatment; a dead man cannot. That is why grace has to be one-directional.
ask: Do I think of salvation as recovery or as resurrection?
Where am I still trying to contribute?

lessons.title: Freely
lessons.teach: 'Justified freely by his grace.' Free does not mean cheap. It means the bill was not sent to us. It was paid elsewhere.
ask: What is the difference between 'free' and 'cheap'?
Have I considered who paid?

lessons.title: Not by works of righteousness
lessons.teach: Even our best deeds are not the ground of salvation. This does not make good works worthless — it moves them from bargaining chip to thank-you.
ask: Are my good works a negotiation or gratitude?
If works do not save, why still live well?

lessons.title: Smote upon his breast
lessons.teach: The man who went home justified was not the morally superior Pharisee but the tax collector who would not lift his eyes. To Jesus' audience this ending was scandalous.
ask: Do I recite a list when I pray?
Is anything needed beyond 'be merciful to me'?

lessons.title: What shall we say then?
lessons.teach: Explain grace properly and this question always follows: 'Shall we sin so grace may abound?' Paul raises it himself — as if a message that never provokes it has not said enough about grace.
ask: Is the gospel I've heard radical enough to raise this question?
Paul's answer was identity, not rules. Why?

lessons.title: The great exchange
lessons.teach: He made him who knew no sin to be sin, that we might become the righteousness of God. This is exchange, not improvement. Not slightly better — a changed standing.
ask: What do I believe God sees when He looks at me?
Am I distinguishing what I am becoming from what I already am?

lessons.title: Grace upon grace
lessons.teach: 'Grace for grace.' Grace is not a one-time entry ticket but a wave that keeps arriving. You do not live today on yesterday's grace.
ask: Do I see grace as an event or a current?
What grace do I need freshly today?

courses.title: What Is Grace
courses.blurb: Seven steps through the word we use most and understand least.

lessons.title: Adam: the first deflection
lessons.teach: 'The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree.' One sentence blaming both his wife and God. The first sin was followed immediately by the first excuse.
ask: Have I examined the grammar of my excuses?
Who am I blaming?

lessons.title: Cain: the man who was warned
lessons.teach: God came to Cain before the murder: 'sin coucheth at the door.' He is not only a judge — He warns first.
ask: When has God tried to stop me?
How did I receive that warning?

lessons.title: Noah: the vineyard after the ark
lessons.teach: The man who endured the flood collapsed in ordinary peacetime. A quiet evening can be more dangerous than a great trial.
ask: Am I weaker in crisis or in calm?
Where am I currently least on guard?

lessons.title: Hagar: the God who sees
lessons.teach: The first person in Scripture to give God a name was not a patriarch but a runaway Egyptian slave: 'Thou God seest me.' The discarded person saw God most clearly.
ask: When have I felt unseen?
What is Hagar's confession in my own words?

lessons.title: Jacob: from taking to holding on
lessons.teach: A lifelong taker finally grabs nothing and simply clings. After that night he walks with a limp. The mark of meeting God was a wound.
ask: Am I still seizing what I should be holding onto?
What is my limp?

lessons.title: Joseph: ye thought evil against me
lessons.teach: Joseph names what his brothers did as evil. He does not soften it. And he says God turned it to good. Forgiveness is not denial of the facts.
ask: What separates forgiving from saying 'it was fine'?
Is there a wound I have not yet named as wrong?

courses.title: People of Genesis
courses.blurb: Reading the patriarchs without the airbrush — who they actually were, and why that is our hope.

lessons.title: How long?
lessons.teach: 'How long' repeats four times. Scripture did not censor this protest; it put it in the songbook. Complaint is a form of prayer.
ask: Do I believe I am allowed to protest to God?
What is my 'how long' right now?

lessons.title: Why hast thou forsaken me?
lessons.teach: Jesus quoted this psalm from the cross. The Son of God said aloud that He felt abandoned by God. That feeling is not a failure of faith.
ask: Have I ever said this out loud?
What changes knowing Jesus used these words?

lessons.title: A broken spirit
lessons.teach: The sacrifice God wants is not flawless performance but a broken and contrite heart. The condition we are most ashamed of is the offering He accepts.
ask: What do I think is worth offering God?
Can I offer my brokenness without hiding it?

lessons.title: My feet were almost gone
lessons.teach: He admits envying the prosperity of the wicked. His perspective changes only when he enters the sanctuary. Place came before answer.
ask: What am I envying?
Has my mind changed by argument, or by worship?

lessons.title: The psalm that ends without hope
lessons.teach: Psalm 88 ends with no comfort: 'mine acquaintance into darkness.' Scripture kept a prayer with no happy ending in the canon. It is allowed to have no answer today.
ask: Do I believe I may speak to God without resolution?
Have I forced a bright ending onto a prayer?

lessons.title: As a weaned child
lessons.teach: One of the shortest psalms. He does not exercise himself in great matters but is quiet like a weaned child with its mother. A weaned child is not there to get something — just to be there.
ask: Do I only come to God to obtain?
Have I ever prayed asking for nothing?

courses.title: Praying the Psalms
courses.blurb: Six psalms for people who lost prayer by only offering tidy prayers.

lessons.title: No condemnation
lessons.teach: The chapter opens with its conclusion. The remaining thirty-nine verses explain this one sentence. The order matters — condemnation does not lift because we improved.
ask: Where am I still condemning myself?
Whose voice is that condemnation?

lessons.title: Abba, Father
lessons.teach: 'Ye have not received the spirit of bondage again to fear.' Faith driven by fear and faith grounded in sonship are different religions.
ask: Is my faith powered by fear or belonging?
Am I comfortable calling God Father?

lessons.title: We know not what we should pray for
lessons.teach: When prayer stalls, the Spirit groans on our behalf. Praying well is not the condition. Wordlessness is part of prayer.
ask: How do I react when I cannot pray?
Have I prayed without words?

lessons.title: All things work together
lessons.teach: Not 'all things are good' but 'all things work together for good.' The verse does not deny pain; it speaks of pain's end. Do not quote it too quickly to a grieving person.
ask: Has this verse ever wounded rather than comforted?
What separates 'works together' from 'it's fine'?

lessons.title: Who shall lay anything to the charge?
lessons.teach: Courtroom language. There may be accusers, but the Judge has already acquitted. And the defense counsel is the one who died and rose.
ask: What does the accusing voice say?
Do I believe the verdict is already in?

lessons.title: Nothing shall separate
lessons.teach: Paul builds a list — death, life, angels, powers, present, future — then adds 'nor any other creature.' He left no loophole. We ourselves are on that list.
ask: What exception am I quietly holding?
What does it mean that even I cannot separate me?

courses.title: Walking Through Romans 8
courses.blurb: One chapter, from no condemnation to a love nothing can sever.

lessons.title: They that are whole
lessons.teach: The religious leaders' question was fair: why eat with tax collectors and sinners? Jesus' answer was not a defense but a definition. Seeking the sick is what a physician is.
ask: Which group do I place myself in?
Why is thinking 'I am well' dangerous?

lessons.title: Neither do I condemn thee
lessons.teach: Jesus did two things at once: He did not condemn, and He named sin as sin. Do only one and you have neither grace nor truth.
ask: Which way do I lean with people?
Is it possible to tell the truth without condemning?

lessons.title: To whom little is forgiven
lessons.teach: 'To whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.' The size of love tracks the size of forgiveness felt. Shrink your sin and your love shrinks with it.
ask: How much do I feel I have been forgiven?
Does that explain the size of my love?

lessons.title: Daughter
lessons.teach: To a woman considered unclean and untouchable for twelve years, Jesus says 'Daughter.' It is the only time in the Gospels He calls anyone that.
ask: What do I think God calls me?
Is an old shame still defining me?

lessons.title: Today shalt thou be with me
lessons.teach: The thief on the cross had no baptism, no service, no time. He made one request. That day he was promised paradise.
ask: If this is the minimum, how does my view of faith change?
What do I still feel I must add?

lessons.title: But some doubted
lessons.teach: Even while worshipping the risen Christ in person, 'some doubted.' And the Great Commission is given to those same people. He assigned the work to doubters.
ask: Do I think doubt disqualifies me from serving?
What obedience am I postponing until I am 100% sure?

courses.title: Encounters in the Gospels
courses.blurb: The list of people Jesus actually spent His time with.
